subject: Cloud Computing
title: The Cost of Cloud Lock-In
description: A short lesson to help you apply The Cost of Cloud Lock-In.

hook.text: A company built everything on AWS Lambda and DynamoDB. Switching providers would cost millions and years.

buildup.text: Lock-in happens when you use proprietary services that don't exist elsewhere. Your code becomes tied to one provider.

discovery.text: Multi-cloud avoids lock-in but adds complexity. Running two clouds is more than twice the operational burden.

twist.text: Some lock-in is intentional. Providers make their unique services irresistibly easy and deeply integrated.

climax.text: The real cost of lock-in isn't the bill — it's lost leverage. You can't threaten to leave if leaving is impossible.

punchline.text: Lock-in starts with convenience. It ends with dependency.

quiz.question: What is the real economic cost of cloud lock-in?
options: Lost negotiating power because switching providers is too costly
Cloud providers charge a penalty fee for being locked in
Lock-in makes cloud services run slower over time

details.summary: Vendor lock-in occurs when using proprietary cloud services that have no equivalent on other platforms. Migrating away requires rewriting code, rearchitecting systems, and paying steep egress fees. The deeper the lock-in, the stronger the provider's negotiating leverage on pricing.
details.whyItMatters: Lock-in reduces your negotiating power and limits strategic flexibility. Understanding which services create lock-in helps make informed decisions about when the tradeoff is worthwhile.
takeaways: Proprietary services create migration barriers and switching costs
Egress fees make data migration expensive at scale
Lock-in gives the provider pricing leverage over your account

faq.question: Which cloud services create the most lock-in?
faq.answer: Proprietary databases like DynamoDB, serverless platforms like Lambda with provider-specific integrations, managed ML services, and IAM systems create the deepest lock-in. Standard services like VMs and object storage are more portable across providers.

faq.question: Is avoiding lock-in always worth the effort?
faq.answer: Not always. Proprietary services often provide superior functionality, lower operational overhead, and faster development. The cost of maintaining cloud-agnostic abstractions can exceed the savings. Accept lock-in strategically where the value justifies the risk.
